title: Trace authority to the exact operation
description: Choose an attack path and an enforcement posture. The trace shows which boundary must reject the request before untrusted input reaches data or a side effect.

stages.label: Session
stages.detail: Validate the session, token issuer, audience, expiry, and revocation state.

stages.label: Route policy
stages.eyebrow: May this role call the operation?
stages.detail: Apply deny-by-default permission checks before expensive work.

stages.label: Object policy
stages.eyebrow: May this caller access this record?
stages.detail: Bind tenant, owner, relationship, and business-state checks to the loaded object.

stages.label: Interpreter boundary
stages.detail: Use parameter binding for commands and contextual encoding for output.

stages.label: State change
stages.eyebrow: Did the user intend this effect?
stages.detail: Verify CSRF evidence, current authorization, limits, and idempotency before committing.

postures.label: Session only
postures.detail: The application trusts any request carrying a valid session.

postures.label: Generic route guard
postures.detail: Authentication and coarse role checks run, but resource and interpreter boundaries are implicit.

postures.label: Operation-scoped enforcement
postures.detail: Identity, route, object, interpreter, and intent checks are explicit at the point of use.

scenarios.label: Change an invoice ID
scenarios.brief: A signed-in user requests an invoice owned by another tenant.
scenarios.safeResult: Return 404 or 403 without revealing whether the foreign invoice exists.
scenarios.unsafeResult: The valid session becomes authority for every invoice identifier.

scenarios.label: Inject a report filter
scenarios.brief: A filter value tries to change the structure of a database query.
scenarios.attackGoal: Turn a bounded report into an unrestricted query
scenarios.safeResult: The driver treats the entire filter as a value and the query structure stays fixed.
scenarios.unsafeResult: String concatenation lets input become executable query syntax.

scenarios.label: Render a stored script
scenarios.brief: A profile field contains markup that executes when another user opens the page.
scenarios.attackGoal: Execute script in another user's trusted origin
scenarios.safeResult: The template encodes the value for its HTML context, so the browser renders text.
scenarios.unsafeResult: Stored data becomes executable markup in every viewer's session.

scenarios.label: Forge a payout request
scenarios.brief: A malicious site submits a state-changing request while the victim is signed in.
scenarios.attackGoal: Reuse ambient session cookies for an unintended transfer
scenarios.safeResult: The server rejects missing or mismatched intent evidence before creating a payout.
scenarios.unsafeResult: A valid cookie is mistaken for proof that the user initiated this transfer.
